newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Flemings says Brazil new phone rates "good news".
newsitem.headline: Flemings says Brazil new phone rates "good news".

text.p: Robert Flemings Securities said that Brazil's telephone rate restructuring was "very good news," because it set rates higher than they had expected.

"It is far more sharp than we had anticipated, meaning that Telebras will better withstand competition when it arrives," analysts William Laurent and Ronald Aitken said in a report. Late on Thursday, Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta announced new tariffs for the telecommunications sector, which should result in an increase in average revenue per line in service of three percent for Telebras, according to Flemings.
The most positive and surprising element of the rate rebalancing was the sharp rise in local and subscription rates, which rose 60 percent and 271 percent respectively, Flemings said.
The monthly resident charge jumped to 13.9 reais from 3.7 reais while the local pulse charge rose to 0.08 reais from 0.05 reais, the report said.
Moreover, international telephone rates fell by an average 17 percent.
Flemings has also reiterated its strong buy rating for Telebras.
The company's revenue is forecast to grow 33 percent this year due to an increase in sales and the rate rebalancing which takes effect Friday, Laurent and Aitken said.
They raised Telebras 1997 net earnings estimates by 5.5 percent to 3.8 billion reais from the previous 3.6 billion reais.
"After the rebalancing, we estimate that all areas of Telebras' activities will be profitable," they said.
The rate increase, designed to eliminate cross-subsidies between long distance and local rates, will also favor some Telebras subsidiaries, they said.
However, the effect will vary among subsidiaries because local and subscription rates rose more than expected, while long distance rates fell more than they forecast, the analysts said.
"The result is that Telerj and Telesp, the most exposed to local telephony, should benefit a lot more than Telepar and, to a lesser extent, Telemig," they said.

Telerj is likely to post "dramatic" improvements in its profitability, which is currently very low. "Telerj remains our favorite subsidiary in Brazil and we strongly reiterate our buy recommendation on the stock," they said.
